title: Wheels, tyres and trim
audience: Car detailers who clean and treat wheels, tyres and exterior trim.
learningOutcomes: Identify the finish of a wheel or trim piece before choosing a product.
Choose a conservative treatment, and refuse an acidic product for an unknown finish with a damaged coating.
Produce a product-compatibility test record before a wider treatment.

instruction.heading: Identify the finish before you choose a product
instruction.body: Wheels and trim come in several finishes, and each responds differently to chemicals. The Auto-Detailing guide separates factory alloy wheels, which often carry a clear coat, from aftermarket or upgraded wheels with a high polish or bare metal, which are more sensitive. Painted alloy, powder-coated wheels, polished lips, and plastic, rubber and vinyl trim each need their own care. Check each wheel in good light and ask the owner where the wheels came from. A wheel with an intact clear coat can be treated much like paint. A polished or bare-metal wheel, or one of unknown origin, should be treated as sensitive until a test shows otherwise. Trim may be unpainted plastic, rubber or vinyl, and a product suited to one may leave a greasy or uneven finish on another. Where the finish is unknown, choose the gentlest approved product, and move up only after a test shows no damage.

instruction.heading: Gentle products and techniques
instruction.body: For most wheels, use a pH-neutral wheel cleaner, or a car shampoo with a dedicated wash media, on wheels that are cool to the touch and in shade. The Auto-Detailing guide says a pH-neutral cleaner can be used on any wheel finish, and that dwell time can be extended in shade for stubborn build-up, following the label. Use soft brushes or natural fibres. A stiff nylon brush can put swirls into a wheel face. Brake dust on a clear-coated wheel may be removed with a clay product, but the Car-Detailing-Guide warns that clay can add marring to a highly polished wheel. Bare-metal lips can be polished with a metal polish after a test. For tyres, water-based dressing soaks into the rubber, while silicone-based dressing sits on the surface, can sling onto the paint, and can dry and brown the rubber over time. Apply tyre dressing in thin, even coats, and keep it off the paint. For trim, clean first and degrease where old polish or wax has built up. Then apply a protectant with UV protection, wiped on with an applicator, and keep it off the paint.

instruction.heading: Refusing an unsuitable product
instruction.body: An acidic wheel cleaner may be proposed for an alloy of unknown finish with a damaged protective coat. The Auto-Detailing guide says acidic cleaners are highly effective but should be used only on factory wheels with a thick clear coat, because they oxidise or tarnish polished and sensitive finishes. A damaged coat leaves metal exposed, and exposed metal is where a product can do the most harm. Refuse the acidic product, choose the gentler approved option, and record the decision and the reason. If the owner insists on the acidic product, decline the treatment in writing rather than accept a risk the business has not assessed. An unidentified product from the bench is not used because it is described as strong. Keep the reasoning on the record.

instruction.heading: Test before a wider treatment
instruction.body: A product-compatibility test is a small trial on an inconspicuous part of the wheel or trim before the wider treatment. Choose an area that is not seen in normal use, such as the inside of the barrel or a spot behind a spoke. Apply the product as its label directs. Record the product, the area, the wait time and the result: no change, a change in colour, a haze, a stain or a loss of gloss. Check the test area after it has dried, not while it is wet, because a product can look fine and then mark. Widen the treatment only when the test shows no damage and the customer has agreed to the work. The Auto-Detailing guide's practice is to test a polish or cleaner on a small area before the entire wheel, and the written record makes that test auditable. Keep the test record with the job file.

procedure: Identify each wheel and trim finish, and record what the owner says about the wheels' origin.
Confirm the wheels are cool and work in shade.
Choose the gentlest approved product for the finish, and read its label for surfaces and dwell time.
Test on an inconspicuous area and record the product, the area, the wait time and the result.
Refuse any product that is unsuitable for the finish, and record the decision.
Widen the treatment only after the test shows no damage and the owner agrees.
Apply tyre dressing in thin coats, and wipe trim protectant on with an applicator, keeping it off the paint.

workedExamples.situation: Aftermarket alloy wheels with a high polish and a scuffed lip. The coating is damaged in two places. The technician is holding an acidic wheel cleaner that was used on factory wheels last week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you use the acidic cleaner?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The finish is unknown and the coating is damaged, so metal is exposed and an acid could etch it and speed corrosion. Refuse the acidic product, choose a pH-neutral approved option, and test it on the inner barrel first. Record the refusal, the reason and the test result.

workedExamples.situation: A test on the inner barrel of painted alloy wheels, using a pH-neutral cleaner and a two-minute wait, shows no change. The owner wants all four wheels done.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you record, and when do you widen the treatment?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the product, the area (inner barrel), the wait time (two minutes), and the result: no change in colour, gloss or texture after drying. Check the test area once it has dried. Widen the treatment to the outer faces of all four wheels only after the owner agrees the work and the test area still looks unchanged after drying. Keep the record with the job file.

equipmentAndPpe: pH-neutral wheel cleaner and a shampoo for light cleaning, both used as their labels direct.
Dedicated wheel wash media, and soft or natural-fibre brushes.
Metal polish for bare metal, used only after a test.
Tyre dressing, water-based or silicone-based as the owner and the label allow.
Trim protectant with UV protection, and applicators.
PPE: gloves and eye protection when using any wheel cleaner, as each SDS requires.

commonErrors.error: Using an acidic cleaner on an unknown finish.
commonErrors.prevention: Identify the finish. Refuse the product if the finish is unknown or the coat is damaged.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning wheels while they are hot.
commonErrors.prevention: Work on cool wheels in shade.

commonErrors.error: Scrubbing with a stiff nylon brush.

commonErrors.prevention: Apply dressing to an applicator in thin coats, and keep it off the paint.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the test before a wider treatment.
commonErrors.prevention: Test, record, let it dry, check, and only then widen the work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wheel cleaners, tyre dressings and trim products have labels and SDSs that set their dilution, dwell time and PPE. A hazardous chemicals register must list each hazardous chemical with its current SDS (Safe Work Australia; the page refers to the model WHS laws of 2011).
Working around wheels can involve splashes and hot surfaces. Working on cool wheels in shade reduces product drying on the surface. This is working practice, not a stated legal requirement.

qualityStandard: The finish of each wheel and trim piece is identified and recorded.
No product is used on a finish it is not labelled for, and each refusal is recorded.
Each wider treatment is preceded by a recorded test with no damage.
documentationEvidence: Finish identification note for each wheel and trim type.
Compatibility test record: product, area, wait time, result, and a check after drying.
summary: Identify the finish before any product is chosen.
Use a pH-neutral product and soft tools unless the finish is known to tolerate more.
Test on a hidden area and record the test before widening the work.

knowledgeChecks.question: A wheel's finish is unknown and its coat is damaged. Which is the right starting point?
options: A pH-neutral approved product, tested on a hidden area first
A strong acid cleaner, since it is safe on any finish
A bleach-based cleaner, because it is quick and kills all the marks
Any product left over from the last job, since it is already open

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a test done on an inconspicuous part of the wheel?
options: To use up the product so nothing goes to waste
To satisfy the owner's curiosity about the product
To check for damage before widening the treatment
To avoid writing a record of the test result

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best way to apply a trim protectant?
options: Wipe it on with an applicator, keeping it off the paint
Spray it straight onto the trim and the paint
Apply it to wet trim in direct sun, so it spreads evenly
Apply a thick coat in one go, so the protection lasts longer
